newsitem.title: USA: Lehman a strong buyout candidate - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Lehman a strong buyout candidate - analyst.

text.p: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc's relatively cheap share price makes it one of the strongest candidates for takeover in the investment banking industry, said Oppenheimer & Co analyst Steven Eisman.

Eisman said Lehman, which is currently trading at below book value, could fetch 1.7 times book value in a takeover, which would translate to about $45 per share, or roughly double its current share price.
Eisman's comments re-iterated those made in a research note issued in late August and included in an item in the September 30 issue of Business Week.
The Business Week article also cited an unidentified New York investment banker who stated talks are underway between Lehman and a New York bank regarding a possible takeover.
A Lehman spokesman was not immediately available to comment and the Business Week article noted that Lehman declined comment on the rumored talks.
Rumors about a possible buyout of Lehman have surfaced repeatedly since the company was spun off from American Express Co in 1994.
As banks are given more leeway to own and operate securites firms, the universe of potential buyers for Lehman expands, Oppenheimer analyst Eisman said in his August research note.
